model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Neal: a Democratic-leaning district, incumbency, and a dominant fundraising position against an independent challenger who has spent beyond what she raised. Markets agree, pricing his win odds near 95%, so the race stays firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: Any credible general-election polling showing the independent challenger within single digits, or a major outside spending push on her behalf, would be the first sign this is closer than fundamentals suggest.

overview:
Richard Neal, a longtime Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a western Massachusetts district that leans Democratic by about eight points. His principal challenger is Nadia Milleron, an independent running as the alternative to the Republican side of the ballot.

Neal holds an overwhelming financial edge, with roughly $3.3 million on hand after raising about $2.5 million, while Milleron has raised about $55,000 and shows negative cash on hand. No public general-election polls are available, but prediction markets price Neal's win probability around 95 percent. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and money makes this a Safe Democratic race, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling rather than any specific evidence of a competitive contest.
